**February 29, 1960 — a Monday, and the rarest of birthdays**

This person arrived on one of the strangest calendar dates in existence. The Gregorian calendar produces a February 29 only in years divisible by four — and only when you were not supposed to exist at all, calendrically speaking. By 2026, at 66 years of lived life, this person has had only 16 actual February 29 birthdays. Every other year, the calendar simply skips them.

---

**The world on this exact day**

The most consequential event of February 29, 1960 was a disaster. At 11:47 PM local time in Morocco, an earthquake struck the coastal city of Agadir. The magnitude was modest — around 5.7 — but the fault was catastrophically shallow, directly beneath the city. By morning, between 12,000 and 15,000 people were dead. One of Morocco's most prosperous and modern cities was effectively erased. It remains among the deadliest earthquakes in African history. The world into which this person was born was, on that very night, witnessing one of the century's sudden catastrophes — a reminder that no decade of human progress comes without nature's indifference running alongside it.

---

**The year itself**

1960 was arguably the most compressed year of transformation in the twentieth century. It was "The Year of Africa": seventeen African nations gained independence from European colonial powers in a single calendar year, permanently redrawing a continent. John F. Kennedy would debate Richard Nixon on television in the autumn — the first televised presidential debate, which changed politics permanently. The Cold War stood at one of its tensest points; the space race between the United States and Soviet Union was less than three years from putting a human in orbit.

This person was born in the final months of the Eisenhower presidency — the last breath of a postwar American order already under severe strain. They would grow up in the Kennedy years, come of age under the shadow of Vietnam, and reach adulthood just as Reagan and Thatcher reshaped the global economy.

---

**A nearby event that shaped the world they entered**

*Twenty-one days after this birth*, on March 21, 1960, South African police opened fire on a crowd of Black demonstrators outside a police station in Sharpeville, killing 69 people and wounding 180 more. The Sharpeville massacre shocked the international community, triggered United Nations condemnation, and permanently accelerated the anti-apartheid movement. It was the moment the world could no longer treat apartheid as a purely internal matter. This person entered the world just three weeks before one of the defining moral crises of the twentieth century forced itself into global consciousness.

---

**The arc of a lifetime**

Growing up in the 1960s meant the Moon landing at age 9, the assassinations of Martin Luther King Jr. and Robert Kennedy at age 8. At 29, the Berlin Wall fell and the Cold War that had defined every year of this person's life simply ended. At 41, September 11. At 49, the first Black president of the United States was inaugurated. At 60, a global pandemic shut down the world. At 66, artificial intelligence had become a daily presence in ordinary life.

The world of February 29, 1960 ran entirely on analog. News came from newspapers and three television channels. Computers occupied entire floors of buildings and were inaccessible to ordinary people. The internet, the personal computer, and the mobile phone did not exist. Intercontinental phone calls required advance booking. The changes this person has lived through in 66 years exceed, in speed and scope, what most prior generations experienced across multiple centuries.

---

**What this birthdate adds up to**

To be born on February 29, 1960, is to arrive at a calendrical anomaly inside a historical one. A city fell to the earth that night. Seventeen nations were weeks away from independence. A political decade unlike any other was just beginning. The person who came into the world on that rare Monday evening grew up to see the entire analog order replaced by a digital one, the Cold War begin and end and be largely forgotten, and the map of Africa transformed entirely from what it looked like the day they were born.

The birthday itself will never be mundane. The world it opened onto was not either.
